# Role binding recipe (v1)

Schema for `.tera/role-bindings/<name>.hcl` recipes per ADR-060 §1. A role binding maps subjects — principals and/or IdP group claims — to a set of roles. At config load, bindings + roles compile to an ordered ACL ruleset. The recipe declares a single `role_binding` block whose label becomes `name`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `recipe/role-binding` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `recipe` — the filename stem is the identity; the file declares exactly one resource, and a block label — where the grammar admits one — must equal the stem (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| Schema `$id` | `https://kottera.dev/schemas/recipe/role-binding/v1` |
| Go source | `github.com/kottera/kottera/pkg/systemvault/schemas.roleBindingRecipe` |
| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/recipe/role-binding/{version}` |
| JSON Schema | `GET /api/v1/schemas/recipe/role-binding/v1` |

## Example

A minimal `role-binding`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/role-bindings/example-role-binding.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

role_binding "example-role-binding" {
  principals = ["worker:example-worker"]
  roles      = ["example-role"]
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes | — | — | const `v1` | Per-recipe grammar version. Required; this schema applies when version is v1. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | Bare binding name (the HCL block label). The loader namespaces it as <vault-id>/role-bindings/<name>. |
| `principals` | string[] | no | — | — | items min length 1 | Explicit principal identities bound to the roles. An entry containing @ is read as a person's email address and is resolved through the user directory at ACL compile time to the opaque tera-issued id a token carries (ADR-135 D2); every other entry is used verbatim. Supports * and prefix* per ADR-010 principal matching. An address no user record carries, or one more than one record claims, is refused by tera config plan and apply when the apply writes the binding (ADR-148 ruling 8); the daemon load still loads such a binding, warns and grants nothing for that address, and an ambiguous address is never resolved by picking one (ADR-135 D11). |
| `idp_group` | string | no | — | — | — | Single IdP group/role claim (OIDC/SAML) bound to the roles: the enterprise golden path (ADR-060 §1). |
| `idp_groups` | string[] | no | — | — | items min length 1 | List form of idp_group. Merged with idp_group when both are present. |
| `guests` | boolean | no | `false` | — | — | The roles reach every guest (ADR-171 D8). A guest holds nothing by default: an allow reaches a guest only when it names the guest class, which this attribute does, or names that guest exactly in principals (an address resolves through the directory to the live guest id). A * or prefix* principal and a group reach no guest. The binding subjects stay the union of principals, the groups and the guest class, and false is the same as not writing it. tera config plan reports, without refusing, a binding with guests = true whose roles grant a wildcard over # or api/v1/# (every guest would hold the operator plane) or grant api/v1/users/invite (which a guest can never use, ADR-171 D6). |
| `roles` | string[] | yes | — | — | min items 1; items min length 1 | Roles granted to the subjects. Bare names resolve against the binding own vault; qualified <vault-id>/roles/<name> references resolve against the named vault. |
